title: Advanced Planetary Orbit Simulator with Scoring
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an advanced planetary orbit simulator using Three.js. Load the 'ABeautifulGame.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.163.0/) and place it at the origin as a decorative centerpiece (scaled to 0.5). Build the following:

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark space background (color: 0x000011)
- Add a bright PointLight at the origin (color: 0xffdd44, intensity: 2.0) to simulate the sun
- Add subtle AmbientLight (intensity: 0.15)
- Camera starts at position (0, 30, 50), looking at origin
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation
- A large glowing yellow sphere (radius 3) at the origin as the 'Sun'

## Planets
- Create 4 planets as colored spheres orbiting the Sun in elliptical orbits using Kepler's laws:
  - Planet 1 (Mercury): radius 0.5, color 0xaaaaaa, semi-major axis 8, eccentricity 0.2, orbital period 3s
  - Planet 2 (Earth): radius 0.8, color 0x2266ff, semi-major axis 14, eccentricity 0.1, orbital period 6s
  - Planet 3 (Mars): radius 0.6, color 0xff4422, semi-major axis 20, eccentricity 0.15, orbital period 9s
  - Planet 4 (Jupiter): radius 1.5, color 0xddaa55, semi-major axis 28, eccentricity 0.05, orbital period 15s
- Each planet leaves a fading orbit trail (use a Line with BufferGeometry, max 200 points per trail)
- Orbital motion: x = a*(cos(E) - e), z = b*sin(E), where b = a*sqrt(1-e^2), and E is eccentric anomaly advancing based on period

## Physics & Simulation
- Implement a time system: simulation runs at timeScale (default 1.0)
- Track elapsed simulation time
- Gravitational constant G can be abstract; orbits are pre-computed ellipses
- Each planet tracks: current angle (true anomaly), distance from sun, orbital velocity (derived from vis-viva: v = sqrt(GM*(2/r - 1/a)))
- Use GM = 1000 for velocity calculations

## Scoring System
- The user earns points by completing educational challenges:
  - 'Identify Fastest': Click the planet closest to the sun (highest velocity). +10 points if correct.
  - 'Predict Position': A ghost marker appears; user must pause and click near where a planet will be in 3 seconds. +20 points if within distance 3.
  - 'Speed Quiz': A DOM prompt asks which planet is fastest right now. +15 points for correct answer.
- Score starts at 0, displayed in HUD
- Challenge mode activated by pressing 'C' key, cycling through challenge types

## User Interactions
- Press SPACE to toggle pause/resume simulation
- Press 'T' to cycle timeScale through [0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0]
- Press 'C' to activate next challenge
- Press 'R' to reset simulation (time=0, score=0, all planets to initial positions)
- Press 'F' to toggle follow-cam mode: camera follows selected planet (cycle with 'N' for next planet)
- Click on a planet (raycasting) to select it and show its info panel
- Press 'O' to toggle orbit trail visibility

## HUD / UI (DOM overlay)
- Top-left: 'Score: X' in large white text
- Top-right: 'Time: Xs | Speed: Xx' showing sim time and timeScale
- Bottom-center: Selected planet info panel showing name, distance from sun, velocity, orbital period
- Center: Challenge prompt text (appears when challenge is active)
- All text uses 'Arial', white color, with semi-transparent dark background panels

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- simulationTime: number (seconds of sim time elapsed)
- timeScale: number (current speed multiplier)
- isPaused: boolean
- score: number
- selectedPlanet: string|null (name of selected planet)
- followMode: boolean
- followTarget: number (index 0-3 of followed planet)
- trailsVisible: boolean
- challengeActive: boolean
- challengeType: string|null ('identify_fastest'|'predict_position'|'speed_quiz'|null)
- challengeCount: number (total challenges completed)
- planets: array of {name, x, z, distanceFromSun, velocity, angle} for each planet
- modelLoaded: boolean (true once ABeautifulGame.glb is loaded)
- planetCount: number (should be 4)
- sunPosition: {x, y, z}

Ensure all numerical values are NaN-free. Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Planets must follow elliptical Keplerian orbits. Orbital velocity follows vis-viva equation v=sqrt(GM*(2/r-1/a)) with GM=1000. Semi-major axes and eccentricities must be preserved. Energy and angular momentum should be approximately conserved. All positions must remain finite and within bounds [-35, 35]. Simulation time must advance monotonically when not paused.
